questions.question: Who decides the salary of state governors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 158(3)** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Governor** is entitled to such emoluments, allowances, and privileges as may be determined by **Parliament** by law.
 
• Until the **Parliament** makes such a law, these emoluments are governed by the provisions specified in the **Second Schedule** of the Constitution.
 
• The **Parliament** enacted the **Governors (Emoluments, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1982**, to regulate these financial aspects. In 2018, the salary of the Governor was significantly increased to **3.5 lakh rupees** per month.
 
• The expenditure for the salary and allowances of the **Governor** is charged upon the **Consolidated Fund of the State**, meaning it is not subject to the vote of the state legislative assembly.
 
• If the same person is appointed as **Governor** of two or more states, the emoluments and allowances payable are allocated among the states in such proportion as the **President** may by order determine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President**:

 
 
• Under **Article 155**, the **President** appoints the **Governor** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• The **Governor** holds office during the **pleasure of the President** as per **Article 156**, but the President does not determine the salary.
 
 
 
• **Finance Commission**:
 
 
• This is a **Constitutional Body** constituted under **Article 280** of the Constitution.
 
• Its primary function is to recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the **Union and the States** and among the states themselves.
 
 
 
• **Salary Immunity**:
 
 
• The **Constitution** ensures that the emoluments and allowances of a **Governor** cannot be diminished during his or her term of office to maintain the independence of the post.

questions.question: Which Ruskin Bond book earned him the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992?

options.text: Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ruskin Bond**, a prolific **Indian author of British descent**, was honored with the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1992** for his literary excellence in **English**.
 
• The award-winning work, **'Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra'**, is a poignant collection of **semi-autobiographical short stories** that vividly capture the author's deep connection with the **Himalayan foothills** and the town of **Dehradun**.
 
• The stories in this collection span several decades of **Bond's life**, reflecting themes of **nature, nostalgia, and the simplicity of life** in the **Garhwal hills**.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi** recognized this work for its **evocative prose** and its ability to portray the **Indian landscape** and its people with immense sensitivity and clarity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Notable Works by Ruskin Bond:**

 
 
• **The Blue Umbrella:** Published in **1980**, this is a beloved children's novel centered on a young girl named **Binya**. It was later adapted into a **National Award-winning film**.
 
• **Angry River:** This was **Bond's first novel written specifically for children**, published in **1972**, featuring the character **Sita** and her struggle against a natural disaster.
 
• **Delhi Is Not Far:** A classic novel that explores the life and aspirations of people in a small town called **Pipalnagar**, highlighting their desire to move to the capital city.
 
• **The Room on the Roof:** His **debut novel**, written at the age of 17, which won the **John Llewellyn Rhys Prize** in **1957**.
 
 
 
• **Major Honors:**
 
 
• Beyond the **Sahitya Akademi Award**, Ruskin Bond was conferred with the **Padma Shri** in **1999** and the **Padma Bhushan** in **2014** for his monumental contributions to **children's literature** and **Indian writing in English**.

questions.question: The Narmada River flows in which direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**East to West**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narmada River** is the largest **west-flowing river** in peninsular India, traversing a distance of approximately **1,312 km**.
 
• It originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in the **Anuppur district** of **Madhya Pradesh** at an elevation of about 1,057 meters.
 
• The river flows through a **Rift Valley** created by down-faulting, situated between the **Vindhya Range** to the north and the **Satpura Range** to the south.
 
• Its drainage basin covers parts of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra**, and **Chhattisgarh**, eventually emptying into the **Arabian Sea** through the **Gulf of Khambhat**.
 
• Unlike most major peninsular rivers that flow towards the east and form deltas, the Narmada flows **East to West** and forms a broad **estuary**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical and Cultural Significance:**

 
 
• It is often referred to as the **Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat** due to its huge contribution to the state economies through irrigation and power.
 
• The **Sardar Sarovar Dam**, one of the largest water resources projects in India, is built across this river in **Gujarat**.
 
• The river creates the famous **Dhuandhar Falls** (Marble Rocks) near **Jabalpur**, where the water plunges over steep rocks.
 
• Major tributaries of the Narmada include the **Hiran**, **Orsang**, **Barna**, and **Kolar** on the right bank, and the **Sher**, **Shakkar**, **Dudhi**, and **Tawa** on the left bank.
 
• The **Tapi River** (Tapti) is the other major river in India that flows in the same **East to West** direction within a rift valley.

questions.question: Which scientist is credited with discovering the neutron in 1932?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Chadwick**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1932**, the British physicist **James Chadwick** discovered the **neutron**, a subatomic particle that carries no electrical charge and has a mass slightly greater than that of a **proton**.
 
• Chadwick conducted an experiment where he bombarded **beryllium** with **alpha particles** emitted from a **polonium** source. This interaction produced a highly penetrating radiation that was not deflected by electric or magnetic fields.
 
• He concluded that this radiation consisted of neutral particles, which he termed **neutrons**. This discovery solved the mystery of why the **atomic mass** of most elements was higher than the combined mass of their protons and electrons.
 
• The identification of the neutron was a pivotal moment in **nuclear physics**, providing the necessary tool for the fission of **uranium-235** and leading directly to the development of the **atomic bomb**.
 
• For his significant contribution to science, **James Chadwick** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1935**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ernest Rutherford**:

 
 
• He is widely known as the **Father of Nuclear Physics** and discovered the **atomic nucleus** in **1911** through the famous **Gold Foil Experiment**.
 
• In **1917**, he performed the first artificial transmutation of an element and is credited with the discovery of the **proton**.
 
 
 
• **Niels Bohr**:
 
 
• In **1913**, he proposed the **Bohr Model** of the atom, which integrated **quantum theory** to describe how electrons revolve in stable, circular orbits around the nucleus.
 
• He explained that electrons can only occupy specific **quantized energy levels**.
 
 
 
• **Wolfgang Pauli**:
 
 
• He was an Austrian theoretical physicist known for formulating the **Pauli Exclusion Principle** in **1925**.
 
• The principle states that no two electrons (or other **fermions**) in an atom can have the same set of four **quantum numbers**.

questions.question: The "Getting Electricity" indicator in the Ease of Doing Business Index (EODB) measures:

options.text: Cost, time, and procedures to obtain electricity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cost, time, and procedures to obtain electricity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Getting Electricity** indicator is a crucial component of the **Ease of Doing Business (EODB) Index**, formerly published annually by the **World Bank Group**.
 
• It measures the efficiency of the public utility in providing a permanent electricity connection to a newly constructed **standardized warehouse**.
 
• The **Procedures** metric tracks every interaction between the business owner and external agencies, such as the **utility company**, government departments, or electrical inspectorates.
 
• The **Time** metric records the number of calendar days required to complete each procedure, from the initial application to the actual flow of electricity.
 
• The **Cost** metric includes all fees associated with the connection, including **security deposits** and costs for external works, expressed as a percentage of the economy’s **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita**.
 
• Since 2015, the indicator also incorporates the **Reliability of Supply and Transparency of Tariffs Index**, which evaluates the frequency and duration of **power outages** (using SAIDI and SAIFI indices).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ease of Doing Business Index**:

 
 
• Launched in **2003**, it ranked 190 economies based on regulatory environments.
 
• Other key indicators included **Starting a Business**, **Registering Property**, and **Resolving Insolvency**.
 
• The report was officially discontinued in **September 2021** following internal audits regarding data integrity.
 
• It has been replaced by a new flagship framework called **Business Ready (B-READY)**, which focuses on the **private sector development** and the overall investment climate.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications**:
 
 
• The **Getting Electricity** data is based on a specific case study: a warehouse with a subscribed capacity of **140 kVA** located in the largest business city of the country.
 
• The connection is assumed to be **low-voltage**, **three-phase**, and **overhead or underground** depending on the local norm.

questions.question: Which Indian solar mission began regular science observations using the SUIT instrument and released its first data sets in early 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aditya-L1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aditya-L1** is India's premier space-based observatory dedicated to studying the **Sun**, launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **September 2, 2023**.
 
• The mission is positioned in a **halo orbit** around the **Lagrangian Point 1 (L1)**, which is situated approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth, providing an unobstructed view of the Sun.
 
• The **Solar Ultra-violet Imaging Telescope (SUIT)** is one of the seven primary payloads on board, designed to capture high-resolution images of the solar **photosphere** and **chromosphere** in the near-ultraviolet (200-400 nm) wavelength range.
 
• In **early 2025**, ISRO transitioned **SUIT** into its regular **science operations phase**, releasing the first comprehensive sets of science data to the global research community for analyzing **solar irradiance** and **space weather**.
 
• The **SUIT** instrument is critical for understanding the coupling and dynamics of the solar atmosphere and measuring the **total solar irradiance** variations that impact Earth's climate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solar Ultra-violet Imaging Telescope (SUIT)**:

 
 
• Developed by the **Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA)**, Pune, in collaboration with various ISRO centers.
 
• It helps in monitoring **solar flares** and **Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs)** that can disrupt satellite communications and power grids on Earth.
 
 
 
• **XPoSat (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite)**:
 
 
• Launched in January 2024, it is India's first dedicated mission to study the **polarization** of cosmic X-rays from sources like **black holes** and **neutron stars**.
 
 
 
• **AstroSat**:
 
 
• India's first multi-wavelength space observatory, launched in **2015**, capable of simultaneous observations in Optical, UV, and X-ray bands.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-3**:
 
 
• A highly successful lunar mission that achieved a historic **soft landing** near the **Lunar South Pole** on August 23, 2023, making India the fourth nation to land on the Moon.

questions.question: When was the Judo Federation of India officially founded and affiliated with the International Judo Federation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1965**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Judo Federation of India (JFI)** was formally established in **1965** to unify various regional groups and standardize the practice of **Judo** across the nation.
 
• Upon its formation in **1965**, the federation immediately sought and obtained official affiliation with the **International Judo Federation (IJF)**, the global authority for the sport.
 
• The **JFI** is also affiliated with the **Judo Union of Asia (JUA)** and is recognized by the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** and the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of India.
 
• The first **National Judo Championship** under the aegis of the **JFI** was organized in **1966** at **Hyderabad**, marking the beginning of organized competitive Judo in India.
 
• Key pioneers like **Sheri N.D. Dewan**, who served as the first General Secretary, played a crucial role in the institutionalization of the federation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution and Significant Milestones:**

 
 
• **Historical Background:** While the federation was formed in **1965**, Judo was introduced to India much earlier; **Rabindranath Tagore** invited a Japanese instructor to **Shantiniketan** in **1905**, and the **Kodokan Judo Academy** was later established in **Mumbai** (then Bombay) in **1929**.
 
• **1986 Seoul Asian Games:** This year was a turning point for Indian Judo as the sport was included for the first time in the **Asian Games**, and Indian judokas secured **four bronze medals**, boosting the federation's prominence.
 
• **Core Functions:** The **JFI** is responsible for conducting technical seminars, grading examinations for **Dan** (Black Belt) rankings, and selecting the national team for international events like the **Commonwealth Games** and the **Olympic Games**.
 
• **Administrative Hub:** The federation operates with its headquarters currently based in **New Delhi**, managing state associations across India to promote the sport at the grassroots level.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the Father of Indian Planning?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M. Visvesvaraya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sir **Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya** was a distinguished **civil engineer** and the 19th **Diwan of Mysore**, serving from 1912 to 1918.
 
• He is celebrated as the **Father of Indian Planning** because he was the first to propose a structured **economic plan** for the nation to combat poverty and underdevelopment.
 
• In 1934, he authored the landmark book **'Planned Economy for India'**, which presented a **ten-year blueprint** for economic development and **industrialization**.
 
• Visvesvaraya famously coined the slogan **'Industrialize or Perish'**, emphasizing that India's survival depended on transitioning from a purely **agrarian society** to an **industrialized economy**.
 
• His contributions to **infrastructure**, including the **Krishna Raja Sagara** dam, and his vision for **technical education** laid the foundation for modern Indian engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji**:

 
 
• Known as the **Grand Old Man of India**, he was a key figure in the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• He authored **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'** and formulated the **Drain of Wealth** theory.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**:
 
 
• The first **Prime Minister** of India and the first Chairman of the **Planning Commission** established in 1950.
 
• He was the architect of the **Mixed Economy** model and advocated for state-led **Socialist planning**.
 
 
 
• **P.C. Mahalanobis**:
 
 
• Regarded as the **Father of Indian Statistics** and founder of the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)**.
 
• He designed the **Mahalanobis Model**, which served as the cornerstone for the **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956–1961), focusing on **heavy industries**.

questions.question: The Industrial Licensing System was introduced in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The industrial licensing system in India was formally established through the enactment of the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (IDRA)** in **1951**, which came into force in **May 1952**.
 
• The primary objective of this act was to provide the **Central Government** with the necessary powers to regulate and develop industries in accordance with national priorities and the objectives set out in the **Five-Year Plans**.
 
• Under the **1951 Act**, a license was mandatory for establishing any new industrial undertaking, manufacturing a **New Article** in an existing plant, or carrying out a substantial expansion of production capacity.
 
• The system was designed to prevent the **Concentration of Economic Power**, protect the interests of **Small-Scale Industries (SSI)**, and ensure **Balanced Regional Development** by incentivizing industries in backward areas.
 
• This regulatory framework formed the core of the **License Permit Raj**, which allowed the state to control the allocation of capital and resources to ensure they served the **Socialistic Pattern of Society**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1948**:

 
 
• This was the first official policy statement after independence, which introduced the concept of a **Mixed Economy** where both the public and private sectors co-existed.
 
• It reserved certain sectors like **Arms and Ammunition**, **Atomic Energy**, and **Railway Transport** exclusively for the state.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956**:
 
 
• Often termed the **Economic Constitution of India**, it expanded the public sector's scope and classified industries into three schedules: **Schedule A** (State monopoly), **Schedule B** (State-led), and **Schedule C** (Private sector).
 
• It emphasized the development of **Heavy and Machine-building Industries** as part of the **Mahalanobis Model** of growth.
 
 
 
• **New Industrial Policy (NIP) 1991**:
 
 
• Marked by the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms, this policy abolished industrial licensing for almost all industries.
 
• Currently, compulsory licensing is limited to only five sectors, including **Defense Equipment**, **Industrial Explosives**, and **Hazardous Chemicals**, primarily for security and safety reasons.

questions.question: What is the name of the artificial intelligence action plan launched by the Indian government in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**INDIA-AI Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IndiaAI Mission** is a comprehensive national-level initiative designed to establish a robust **Artificial Intelligence ecosystem** in India by fostering innovation and ensuring technological sovereignty.
 
• A primary objective of the mission is the creation of a massive **AI Computing Infrastructure**, which involves the deployment of over **10,000 Graphics Processing Units (GPUs)** through public-private partnerships to support startups and researchers.
 
• The mission establishes the **IndiaAI Datasets Platform**, which acts as a central repository for high-quality, non-personal datasets to help Indian developers train advanced AI models.
 
• It focuses on indigenous development through the **IndiaAI Innovation Centre**, which is tasked with building **Large Multimodal Models (LMMs)** and foundational models specifically tailored to Indian languages and sectors like agriculture and healthcare.
 
• The framework aims to democratize AI benefits by supporting **Deep-Tech startups** and integrating AI education into the national curriculum to bridge the digital talent gap.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Allocation and Governance**:

 
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by the Prime Minister, approved a total financial outlay of **₹10,372.92 crore** for this mission.
 
• The mission is implemented by the **'IndiaAI' Independent Business Division (IBD)** under the **Digital India Corporation** (DIC) within the Ministry of Electronics and IT.
 
 
 
• **Key Pillars**:
 
 
• **IndiaAI FutureSkills**: This component focuses on creating **AI-ready vocational courses** and establishing Data and AI Labs in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
 
• **Safe & Trusted AI**: This pillar ensures the development of **ethical AI frameworks**, focusing on bias mitigation and establishing guardrails for responsible deployment.
 
• **IndiaAI Startup Financing**: Provides streamlined access to capital for early-stage **deep-tech AI firms** to accelerate commercialization.

questions.question: Which scheme provides financial incentives to promote exports from SEZs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)** was introduced in the **Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2015-20** to promote the export of notified goods produced in India.
 
• The scheme specifically includes **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)** units, making them eligible for financial rewards to offset infrastructural inefficiencies and associated costs involved in exporting.
 
• Incentives under MEIS are provided in the form of **Duty Credit Scrips**, which are calculated as a percentage (usually **2% to 7%**) of the realized **Free on Board (FOB)** value of exports in free foreign exchange.
 
• The scheme consolidated five earlier incentive programs, such as the **Focus Product Scheme (FPS)** and **Market Linked Focus Product Scheme (MLFPS)**, into a single unified framework to simplify the process for exporters.
 
• By providing these incentives, the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** aimed to enhance the **global competitiveness** of Indian manufactured goods and increase India’s share in world trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Duty Credit Scrips**:

 
 
• These are **freely transferable** instruments that can be used to pay **Basic Customs Duty** on the import of inputs, capital goods, or other notified items.
 
• If an exporter cannot use the scrips for their own imports, they can be sold in the **secondary market** at a premium.
 
 
 
• **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)**:
 
 
• Governed by the **SEZ Act, 2005**, these zones are treated as **foreign territories** for trade operations and duties, offering tax holidays and simplified procedures.
 
• Units in SEZs enjoy **100% Income Tax exemption** on export income for the first 5 years under **Section 10AA** of the Income Tax Act.
 
 
 
• **Transition to RoDTEP**:
 
 
• To align with **World Trade Organization (WTO)** requirements regarding export subsidies, the MEIS was replaced by the **Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP)** scheme effective from **January 1, 2021**.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024-25** (presented in July 2024) provides a comprehensive analysis of the **General Government** expenditure, which includes the combined spending of the **Central Government** and **State Governments**.
 
• According to the survey data, the total expenditure on **Social Services** has grown at a **Compounded Annual Growth Rate (CAGR)** of **15%** during the period from **FY 2021** to **FY 2025 (Budget Estimates)**.
 
• Social services expenditure primarily consists of three major heads: **Education**, **Health**, and **Other Social Sectors** (which covers housing, water supply, and sanitation).
 
• In absolute terms, the spending on social services increased significantly from **₹12.8 lakh crore** in **FY 2019** to approximately **₹21.3 lakh crore** in **FY 2023 (Revised Estimates)**, maintaining a robust trajectory through the **FY 2025** budget.
 
• The share of **Social Services** expenditure as a percentage of the total **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** has remained stable at around **6.7%** to **7.8%** over this period, highlighting the government’s commitment to social welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Health Sector Focus**:

 
 
• The **Health** expenditure share within the social services segment saw a notable rise, driven by post-pandemic infrastructure strengthening and the expansion of the **Ayushman Bharat** scheme.
 
 
 
• **Education Sector Trends**:
 
 
• Investment in **Education** remains the largest component of social sector spending, with a renewed focus on the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020** and digital learning initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Priorities**:
 
 
• The **15%** growth reflects the transition from crisis-response spending in **FY 2021** to long-term **Social Infrastructure** development, ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reach the vulnerable sections of society.

questions.question: Along with whom did Rani Lakshmi Bai fight with the British in Jhansi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tantia Tope**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rani Lakshmi Bai**, the legendary queen of the princely state of **Jhansi**, was a central figure in the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, resisting British annexation under the **Doctrine of Lapse**.
 
• When the **British forces**, commanded by **Sir Hugh Rose**, besieged the **Jhansi Fort** in **March 1858**, the Rani led a fierce defense of her territory.
 
• **Tantia Tope**, a highly skilled general and close associate of **Nana Saheb**, marched with an army of approximately **20,000 men** to assist the Rani and relieve the siege at **Jhansi**.
 
• Despite the defeat at the **Battle of Betwa**, **Tantia Tope** and **Rani Lakshmi Bai** successfully coordinated their escape and retreated toward **Kalpi**.
 
• The two leaders, along with **Rao Sahib**, executed a daring plan to capture the **Gwalior Fort** from the **Scindia** rulers, who remained loyal to the **British**, making it a major stronghold for the rebel forces.
 
• The partnership between **Rani Lakshmi Bai** and **Tantia Tope** represented one of the most significant military alliances during the **First War of Independence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tantia Tope**:

 
 
• His original name was **Ramachandra Panduranga** and he was born in **Yeola**, Maharashtra.
 
• He was known for his expertise in **guerrilla warfare** and continued the struggle against the **British** in the jungles of **Central India** until his capture and execution in **April 1859**.
 
 
 
• **Begum Hazrat Mahal**:
 
 
• She was the wife of **Nawab Wajid Ali Shah** and took charge of the rebellion in **Lucknow** (Awadh).
 
• She declared her son, **Birjis Qadr**, as the Wali of **Awadh** and organized resistance against **Sir Henry Lawrence**.
 
 
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar**:
 
 
• The last **Mughal Emperor** of India, he was proclaimed the **Shahenshah-e-Hindustan** by the sepoys in **Delhi** during the **1857 Revolt**.
 
• He was later tried for treason and exiled to **Rangoon**, Burma, by the **British**.
 
 
 
• **Rani Avantibai Lodhi**:
 
 
• The queen of **Ramgarh** (Mandla district), she raised an army of **4,000** to fight the **British** and is remembered for her sacrifice in the **Central Provinces**.

questions.question: What was the name of the army formed by Subhas Chandra Bose to fight for India's independence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Army (INA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Army (INA)**, also known as the **Azad Hind Fauj**, was an armed force formed by Indian nationalists in **1942** in **Southeast Asia** during **World War II**.
 
• While the army was initially conceived by **Captain Mohan Singh** with the assistance of the **Japanese**, it was later reorganized and revitalized under the leadership of **Subhas Chandra Bose** after his arrival in **Singapore** in **July 1943**.
 
• The primary objective of the **INA** was to liberate India from **British colonial rule** through an armed struggle, operating in conjunction with the **Japanese Imperial Army** during the **Burma Campaign**.
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** assumed the role of **Supreme Commander** of the army and established the **Provisional Government of Free India** (Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind) in **October 1943**.
 
• Under Netaji's leadership, the **INA** consisted of various regiments named after prominent leaders like **Gandhi**, **Nehru**, and **Azad**, symbolizing a united front for **National Independence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure and Special Units:**

 
 
• The **INA** was unique for its time as it featured a dedicated all-female combat unit known as the **Rani of Jhansi Regiment**, commanded by **Captain Lakshmi Sahgal**.
 
• The force was largely composed of **Indian Prisoners of War (POWs)** who had been captured by the **Japanese** after the **fall of Singapore** in **1942**.
 
 
 
• **Famous Slogans and Legacy:**
 
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** motivated his troops with the powerful slogan **Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom**.
 
• The **Red Fort Trials** of **1945**, where **INA** officers were prosecuted by the British, triggered massive public demonstrations and significantly weakened the **British Raj's** control over the **Indian military**.
